newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian officials fly to Baku, pipeline deal seen.
newsitem.headline: Russian officials fly to Baku, pipeline deal seen.

text.p: A high-level Russian delegation flew to the Azeri capital Baku on Friday, where officials said they were likely to sign a long-stalled deal on transporting Caspian oil through Russia's breakaway Chechnya republic.
The delegates were scheduled to meet Azeri President Haydar Aliyev later on Friday and Azeri officials said a deal might be signed in the evening or in the next few days.
Energy Minister and First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov flew from Moscow with Deputy Energy Minister Yevgeny Morozov, Itar-Tass news agency said.

Boris Agapov and Boris Berezovsky, deputy secretaries of Russia's Security Council, were also in the delegation, it said, adding that an Energy Ministry representative would sign any transport deal on Russia's behalf.
The deal is meant to sort out how revenues will be shared from the transport of the oil, which is to be produced by an $8 billion international consortium in the Azeri sector of the Caspian Sea.
The oil will be pumped along a pipeline which runs through Chechnya.
But the southern separatist region of Chechnya, which fought a bloody, 21-month war with Moscow in a failed secession bid, is playing its card by demanding a share in profits from the transport.
On Friday progress was made in resolving remaining problems in relations with the signing of banking and customs agreements between Moscow and the Chechen capital Grozny.
Berezovsky said Friday's deals "laid the basis for the economic revival of the Chechen republic".
